approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored current molecule by sampling local graph edits, including a direct exchange of aromatic nitrogen and carbon that preserves molecular formula. It normalizes identities, rejects duplicates and fills each batch with the first neighbors admitted by its inverse-motif memory. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes current even when its score is worse, while an independent archive retains the best observations. Memory blocks only qualifying two-sign reversals from one selected transition; partial reversals can remain admissible. When accepted neighbors tie for the maximum score, canonical spelling currently decides which becomes the next source.
approach.novelty: Among equally best accepted neighbors, prefer the one that undoes the fewest motif-occurrence changes from the immediately previous selected transition, then use canonical order if that comparison also ties. This gives the most recent structural direction a chance to persist at the same accepted score. Earlier tie-selection siblings preferred fewer heavy atoms or greater distance from the current molecule. This rule instead compares the directions and magnitudes of two consecutive moves; it can prefer less structural displacement and does not reward compactness. The existing proposal generator and memory restrictions remain the Parent's.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-abcd951ab7cc completes its prescribed panel with macro mean 0.5217591163770486 and population deviation 0.006329100643035156; its actual per-seed summary.json and run.log files agree on completion. Its lexical maximum-tie rule can choose a partial reversal of the immediately previous selected transition even when another actually accepted maximum reverses fewer motif occurrences. The passive audit .slots/SPIRAL2.r0012-09-improve-L16.plan-reversal-audit.json joins every one of 4350 accepted molecules to its emission, graph-derived inherited motif counts, source, trajectory score and selected transition. All 214232 checks pass. Of 435 transitions, 409 have unique maxima and 26 have exact ties containing 64 maximizers. Twelve tie sets contain any inverse overlap with the previous transition; nine have unequal overlap counts. Minimizing the registered capped overlap would change four lexical winners, reducing the total overlap across tied winners from 13 to six occurrences. All four are source-score plateaus: median_2 seed 1 batch 12 and deco_hop seed 2 batches 9, 13 and 29. The last is terminal; only three have later proposal opportunities. These are conditional comparisons on the actual Parent history, not a reconstructed alternative walk. The rule differs from source-distance selection on nine Parent tie sets and from minimum-size selection on seven; three changed choices preserve the lexical winner's heavy-atom count and the terminal choice has two more atoms. The source-distance sibling n-4341f3da1e57 changed 20 real winners but lost 0.0018116198229683282 in paired macro mean, and the size siblings n-770a3cefca6a and n-d4f4384cd477 report the same six changes and paired loss 0.0011038146568116785, not independent replications. Their evidence motivates testing persistence of the previous move's motif changes rather than another source-distance or size preference. It does not establish that avoiding a partial reversal improves subsequent scores.
hypothesis: Among exact accepted-score batch maxima, select the neighbor with the smallest capped inverse motif-occurrence overlap with the immediately previous selected transition, then use canonical lexical order for any remaining tie.

finding_summary.headline: Five tied choices reduced immediate motif overlap, but the predicted score gain did not appear
finding_summary.insights: This rules out failure to execute the tie rule as the explanation for the absent score gain. Reducing immediate motif-count reversal can change the search without shortening its plateaus or improving its aggregate endpoint. The five choices overlap within only two task/seed continuations, so the later deco_hop improvement cannot be credited independently to each of its four changed ties. The count statistic also has a narrower chemical meaning than preserving the last physical edit: it can penalize extending an ethyl group to propyl, or match a motif lost on one ring to a motif introduced on another. One changed choice preserves a C#S-O group by extending an unrelated N-alkyl chain, while another replaces a carbonyl carbon with sulfur. The molecular assessment finds that the altered paths retain or add questionable sulfur, oxygen-oxygen and sulfur-halogen connections, with no change to the pooled highest-scoring molecule on any task. Lower overlap therefore supplies no evidence of improved feasibility or more useful chemistry. Whether a comparison tied to actual edited sites or chemically useful arrangements would improve these choices remains open.
finding_summary.results: The rule changed five of 26 tied maximum decisions across two of fifteen task/seed sessions. Each change kept the same accepted score and reduced overlap with the previous move to zero; the corresponding lexical choices would have reversed eight motif occurrences in total. All five choices had later evaluations. Across the complete walks, inverse overlap during score plateaus fell from 26 to 14 occurrences, yet plateau transitions increased from 49 to 52. The three-seed macro mean was 0.52169764, compared with 0.52175912 for the parent: a paired change of -0.00006147, below the predeclared +0.002 improvement. The changed deco_hop continuation finished at 0.61072664 versus 0.60921826, while median_2 finished at 0.18849201 versus 0.19092251. The other thirteen full molecule/score trajectories were identical. The local mechanism is confirmed; the predicted score benefit is refuted.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic and carbonyl families repeatedly acquire unusual sulfur, reactive attachments and dense cages with unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: Node n-1aba3c4825a4 produces medium-sized to large, heavily substituted ring systems: recognizable indole/benzofuran carboxamides, aryl ketones, fused nitrogen heterocycles, cyclic amines and lactams coexist with much less conventional sulfur-rich cages. Each supplied task digest covers 900 evaluated rows, including 870 optimizer proposals over seeds 0, 1 and 2. Ring-closure-token presence is 1.0 in every proposal set. Aromatic-token presence in the fixed task order is 0.9563, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 and 0.7184; these are molecule-presence rates, not fractions of aromatic atoms. Every task has charged-token and stereocentre-token rates of 0.0. The neutral spelling does not imply absence of potentially basic amines. Passive RDKit reading of the full supplied trajectories confirms ring and aromatic content and graph parseability, but does not establish conformational feasibility, chemical stability or synthesis. Structural diversity is moderate: different seeds reach different ring families, while the displayed score leaders often cluster around one heavily modified framework. Direct Child/Parent comparison finds identical molecule/score records in thirteen of fifteen task/seed trajectories. The differences are confined to deco_hop seed 2 and median_2 seed 1; the highest-scoring molecule pooled over seeds remains identical to the Parent on every task. The changed trajectories introduce different chemistry without resolving the recurring liabilities. All five objectives have trajectories. Size, bond-prevalence and Parent comparisons below are passive counts from those files, recorded in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0012-09-improve-L16.molecular-audit.json. Score readings describe observed molecular associations and do not infer an unseen target structure, activity mechanism or score for an unobserved analogue.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer proposals contain 21-29 heavy atoms and 2-6 RDKit-perceived rings. The displayed leaders are relatively compact fused heteroaromatic/phenyl carbonyl compounds. The seed-1 indole carboxamide at evaluation 61 has ethoxy, methyl and thiol substituents and scores 0.39905049777278273; its indole/anilide connectivity is comparatively recognizable synthetic chemistry. The overall leader at seed 2 evaluation 133, score 0.41003927643747895, is a benzofuran carboxamide carrying an aminophenyl group, an N-chloro amide, methyl substituents, a thiol and a carbon bearing both amino and chloro substituents. The seed-0 leader is a benzothiophene aryl ketone with an aminomethyl ether and chloromethyl group, score 0.393567030299894. Later products also include bridged unsaturated rings and substituted sulfur. All three complete molecule/score trajectories match the Parent, so these recognizable motifs and the less plausible derivatives are inherited output chemistry.
liabilities: The leading N-chloro amide and carbon bearing both amino and chloro substituents are chemically less reassuring than the ordinary anilide; thiol and chloromethyl groups also introduce reactivity concerns.

Other cited molecules contain N-F/N-O or N-N connections, and late unsaturated sulfur bridges require structural and synthetic scrutiny. These concerns do not apply indiscriminately to normal thiophene or amide functionality.
Ring-rich low scorers show that adding or distorting rings does not by itself preserve the favorable chemical arrangement.
missing_features: Consistent retention of the compact fused-aromatic/carbonyl/phenyl arrangement during scaffold changes: several lower-scoring products disrupt aromaticity or the carbonyl connection.

Broader coverage of conventional, less reactive variants of the same successful aryl-carbonyl arrangements; ordinary indole amide chemistry already appears among the leaders, but reactive N-halogen and benzylic attachments recur.
Defined stereochemical identities for the substituted saturated and bridged products. The records establish absent specification, not a demonstrated score reward for adding it.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145, and the displayed aromatic carbonyl leaders reach 0.393567030299894-0.41003927643747895. A low-scoring indole derivative with a tetrahedral linker replacing the carbonyl arrangement scores 0.03343008011310944, while the expanded, partly dearomatized ring system at seed 0 evaluation 242 scores 0.021532846118034143. These are consistent with a useful compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement, although the comparisons change other features too. The chloro and bromo versions of one bridged anilide both score 0.3900523103411983, so those observations do not distinguish the halogen identity. The final seed-2 sulfur/N-N cage derivative scores 0.3852230774700024. Its score and the N-chloro leader show tolerance of questionable attachments; they do not establish that such attachments are required.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals contain 30-53 heavy atoms, with aromatic-token presence 1.0. They retain substituted aromatic and fused nitrogen-heterocyclic cores while accumulating alkyl, ether, imine/imidate, carbonyl/thione and sulfur-containing appendages. The overall leader, score 0.6161710037174721, has 51 heavy atoms: a densely substituted aryl group, a fused nitrogen heterocycle, a thione and carbonyl, N-Br, a carbon bearing F and an amino linkage, and a long ether/thioether-containing chain attached through additionally substituted sulfur. This is a crowded and chemically questionable assemblage. Seed 2 differs from the Parent from evaluation 101 onward. Its later products instead display an imidate-bearing aza/O ring system linked to a dioxo nitrogen heterocycle and an O-O/N-O-containing ring with a fused triangular carbon ring. The Parent continuation has more conspicuous polyene/acetal appendages. Across the 870 optimizer rows, O-O bonds occur in 89 Child rows versus 11 Parent rows. This is a bond-presence count; successful aromatic perception does not certify those oxygen-rich ring structures.
liabilities: The leading family combines substantial size and flexible appendages with N-halogen bonding and nonstandard substituted sulfur multiple-bond environments.
The changed seed-2 family introduces an O-O-connected heterocycle fused to a triangular carbon ring. Its unusual conjugation and geometry remain unresolved despite graph validity.
No stereochemistry is specified even where the branched fluorinated carbons and substituted rings permit stereogenic distinctions.
missing_features: Chemically ordinary alternatives that retain the aryl/fused-polar-ring arrangement without the long, reactive and partly score-indistinguishable decorations.
Feasible oxygen/nitrogen ring replacements preserving the observed polar-group placement without the unusual O-O/N-O ring and fused triangular carbon topology.
Matched simplifications sufficient to establish which appendages matter. The displayed equal scores support testing this gap but do not identify a unique missing target scaffold.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial phenolic ester/fused dioxo heterocycle scores 0.548381482770623, while a disrupted, constrained nitrogen-ring variant scores 0.526081691583997. The displayed decorated aryl/heterocycle leaders reach 0.6161710037174721. Several closely related molecules all score 0.6155070237050044 despite alkyl extension or replacement of N-methyl by N-bromo. The recorded plateau supplies no evidence that those extra atoms or the N-Br bond are necessary. In the changed seed-2 trajectory, the recorded maximum is 0.610726643598616 versus the Parent maximum 0.6092182584436399; the digest shows a related late dioxo/aromatic compound at 0.6097959509006855 and a ring-expanded carbonyl relative at 0.5832771733898142. per_task.generated_character: The proposals contain 32-43 heavy atoms and 2-9 perceived rings. Aromatic-token presence is 1.0 and halogen-token presence is 0.9966. The high-scoring molecules combine phenyl/phenol groups, halogenated aryl groups, cyclic amines and primary aminomethyl substituents with sulfur-rich, partly saturated rings. The overall leader at 0.9148143511682032 has a methylphenol and chlorophenyl group, a tertiary cyclic nitrogen, an aminomethyl substituent and a multiply bonded sulfur-sulfur bridge. Another leader at 0.8856242185485628 contains an aziridine, a larger nitrogen ring, halogenated aryl groups and thiocarbonyl/sulfur functionality. Basic amine functionality is visibly present; all molecules are nevertheless written without explicit formal charge. All three complete molecule/score trajectories match the Parent. The aromatic/amine-rich chemistry and unusual sulfur environments therefore persist unchanged.
liabilities: Multiply bonded sulfur-sulfur units and additionally substituted sulfur occur in leading structures; the large recorded scores do not establish chemical stability or real binding.
The aziridine-containing leader and densely linked ring systems add strain and synthesis concerns. Their structures are graph-valid but have no demonstrated feasible configuration here.
Every optimizer row has an unassigned stereogenic centre under passive RDKit perception, consistent with the digest stereocentre-token rate of 0.0.
missing_features: Conventional saturated aza-ring and linker alternatives preserving the observed amine/aryl spacing while avoiding sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds and highly unusual sulfur coordination.
Stable matched replacements for the nonstandard sulfur bridges, which would clarify whether the favorable molecular arrangement survives in more credible chemistry.
Specified configurations for the substituted small rings and crowded cyclic amines. Their stereochemical and protonation-state consequences are unresolved by these neutral, unassigned structures.

The leading later structures instead expose aliphatic amine centres and differently spaced aryl groups, generally without those carbonyl/acid groups. This is a broad trajectory association, not an isolated proof about acidity or binding. A closer displayed comparison retains an intervening methylene in the nitrogen-to-sulfur-ring connection at 0.8663008496126992; the direct N-S-connected relative scores 0.3331237338421948. Replacing an aminomethyl group by an O-N-containing branch gives 0.5308080684367313, and replacing one phenyl ring by an unsaturated sulfur ring gives 0.04252669549740123. per_task.generated_character: The proposals contain 27-45 heavy atoms and 3-8 perceived rings, with aromatic-token presence 1.0. The displayed leaders are bridged aromatic/aliphatic lactam frameworks containing a pyridine ring, a phenyl group, alkyl substituents and an N-O ring closure. The overall leader at 0.21196904390980506 has 31 heavy atoms and a densely interconnected medium-ring topology. It is not simply a flat aromatic molecule: much of its complexity is in the bridges around the lactam and unsaturated carbon framework. liabilities: The bridged leaders require unresolved medium-ring geometry and stereochemistry; an N-O bond in this cage context needs specific assessment rather than a blanket assumption of stability.
Cited relatives contain N-N and O-O connections with little score separation from carbon-linked variants.
The changed trajectory adds S-Br and retains O-Br attachments and unusual sulfur coordination. These are reactive-bond liabilities rather than evidence of useful scaffold diversity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A conventional indole carboxamide reaches 0.39905049777278273, while related leading chemistry also includes an N-chloro amide at 0.41003927643747895. Displayed carbon/sulfur ring variants tie at 0.8825461379136246 or 0.8663008496126992. One changed proposal set contains O-O bonds in 89 of 870 rows versus 11 Parent rows, and another contains sulfur-halogen bonds in 142 of 870 rows versus 25 Parent rows. These observations do not demonstrate a chemical requirement for the reactive bonds.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently separate useful aryl, amine and carbonyl arrangements from reactive attachments and nonstandard sulfur connectivity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide matched conventional linkers and heteroatom environments while preserving the useful fragment arrangement, and let observed feedback establish which replacements remain useful. Distinguish ordinary thiophenes, thioethers, carbonyl derivatives and carbon-bound halogens from heteroatom-halogen bonds, peroxide-like connections and unusually coordinated or multiply bonded sulfur.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Several decorated heterocycles share 0.6155070237050044 despite alkyl extension and N-methyl-to-N-bromo substitution. Carbon/nitrogen connection variants share 0.20775769309691736, and an O-O-containing relative scores 0.20647766243219587. The recorded identities differ, but those score comparisons provide little evidence for the extra branch size or reactive connections.
transferable_gaps.gap: Matched simplification of peripheral branches and heteroatom connections is underrepresented relative to elaborate, score-indistinguishable derivatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Include coherent matched simplifications of side chains and connectors while preserving the principal ring and polar-group arrangement. Use accepted feedback to determine which reduced structures retain the observed benefit; the evidence does not justify indiscriminate deletion or treating molecular size as a substitute for the objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A methylene-linked nitrogen/sulfur-ring arrangement scores 0.8663008496126992 while its direct N-S relative scores 0.3331237338421948. A carbonyl-to-imino replacement changes 0.519850349488241 to 0.48440391849409126 within a fluorinated cage. Ring-opened carbonyl-chain molecules score 0.12467972074136988 and 0.1263981386214515, below the displayed constrained aromatic/lactam family. Rings and heteroatoms are abundant; the missing capability is reliable preservation of their useful relationships.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring and linker changes do not consistently preserve the spacing and polar-group identity associated with stronger molecular scores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Broaden access to feasible ring sizes, ordinary aza/oxa frameworks and linker-length alternatives that retain the other aryl and polar-group attachments. Use local matched variations to distinguish the contribution of spacing from simultaneous changes in aromaticity, carbonyl identity and ring congestion.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every supplied proposal set has stereocentre-token rate 0.0. The cited structures include substituted cyclic amines, an aziridine, bridged lactams, triangular carbon rings and densely connected fluorinated sulfur cages. These are the same unassigned leading structures found in the Parent; a successful graph parse does not specify a realizable configuration.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator supplies no stereochemical specification for many substituted rings and cages whose geometric identities remain unresolved.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and preserve feasible stereogenic configurations where the generated graph supports them, and broaden access to less congested alternatives with comparable fragment placement. Treat geometric feasibility and configurational identity as explicit chemical questions. The present trajectories establish the coverage gap without establishing a score gain from stereochemical assignment.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
